positive_controls.argument: Architecture analysis identifies the coupled interface and quality constraints that targeted restructuring must preserve, and separates the expensive seam from local reversible details.
Observed configuration and environment correspondence determine whether the restructuring evidence concerns the maintained object and reveal drift that defeats a claimed preserved behavior.

The qualification envelope specifies which timing, resource and environmental properties a proposed behavior-preserving change must retain or re-examine, giving a concrete boundary to technical improvement.
Hazard scenarios and control dependencies identify the consequential behaviors and interactions that must survive structural work and make some apparently local changes safety-relevant.
The actual data, environment, operator and contingency requirements of cutover define which structural changes are needed now and which polishing can be deferred.
Recovery tests reveal which current-state assumptions, dependencies and inaccessible seams obstruct repair, supplying concrete priorities and acceptance conditions for changeability investment.
Support horizon, likely replacements, supplier rights and retirement plans identify which change options have value and which debt can rationally remain until retirement.
The consequence, coupling, recovery and obligation profile bounds the verification and authority needed for the structural change, preserving a cheap existing path where it is adequate.
The rejection of an unrestricted phase curve removes an invalid automatic justification for preventive restructuring and requires comparison with the anticipated change and other cost components.
